messages:
cecilia: Heads-up — dashboard alarm spiked for hosted-usw2 GPU pool p95 queueing around 08:12 UTC, looks sustained for ~20m :thinking:
infra-bot: Alert: gpu_pool_usw2_saturation fired (p95_queue_ms > 1200ms) — 08:12:05 UTC
mike: Seeing same in logs, admission control started rejecting bursty requests, rate limit 100r/s per customer tripped for a few tenants :warning:
ashok: Any config changes recently to batching or max_concurrency for that pool? I didn't push anything this morning.
samir: Not from infra side. Product rolled a canary that increased max_tokens default for chat endpoints ~2 hours ago — could be correlated.
cecilia: That matches timing. We should confirm token distribution — bigger requests increase KV cache pressure and lower throughput.
mike: Query I ran: `sum(rate(requests[5m])) by (pool) > 100` + `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(queue_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,pool))` — p95 shows 1.3s for usw2-hosted.
ashok: Can we temporarily bump burst capacity in usw2? ETA to spin up extra instances if we use spot-burst is ~6-8m.
samir: We have windfall credits but need to be mindful of cost. If we enable burst, cost estimate ~+$2k/day. Should we fallback some tenants to euw1 to relieve pressure?
cecilia: Yes, good idea. Plan: 1) Enable short burst for 15m, 2) Route a few large tenants to euw1, 3) Add alert for token-size skew. Who can run the burst? @mike
mike: I'll trigger burst now. Command:
```
infractl pool burst --pool=hosted-usw2 --instances=6 --type=spot --duration=900
```
mike: Running it — provisioning started (instances requested). Will post when healthy.
infra-bot: Pool action: burst requested by mike — 6 spot instances (expires in 900s)
sre-oncall: Noted. I'll throttle non-critical background jobs in usw2 to free headroom — removing batch-async jobs for 10m.
ashok: Routing change: updating routing policy to prefer euw1 for tenant IDs in the large-tenants list, adding soft-fallback.
cecilia: Also adding a short-term admission rule: cap tokens/request to 4k for hosted-usw2 to keep median latency stable. We should measure QoE impact.
samir: Agree. Add an Eval run to track quality regressions for those tenants over next 2 hours.
mike: Burst instances are healthy, GPU utilization dropped 18% and queue p95 now ~720ms — looks effective :thumbsup:
cecilia: Great. Keep burst for 15m then scale down if stable. Next actions: add dashboard panel for token size distribution, and new alert: sustained p95 > 1s for >10m and tenant_token_95p > 2000 => page.
ashok: I'll push the dashboard change to grafana and add the alert rule now.
sre-oncall: Log note for postmortem: incident due to product change increasing default tokens; consider rollout guard for defaults that impact throughput.
cecilia: Thanks team. After scale-down, let's sync tomorrow on automated routing policies and cost cap guards. :coffee:
